{{Short description|Mathematical constant}}
{{Use shortened footnotes|date=May 2021}}  
In [[number theory]], '''Niven's constant''', named after [[Ivan Niven]], is the largest exponent appearing in the [[prime factorization]] of a [[natural number]] "on average". More precisely, if we set <math>H(1) = 1</math> and define <math>H(n)</math> to be the largest exponent appearing in the prime factorization of <math>n > 1</math>, then Niven's constant is given by

:<math>
\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{j=1}^n H(j) = 1+\sum_{k=2}^\infty \bigg(1-\frac{1}{\zeta(k)}\bigg) 
= 1.7052111401\dots
</math>

where <math>\zeta</math> is the [[Riemann zeta function]].{{sfnp|Niven|1969}} Niven also proved that

:<math>
\sum_{j=1}^n h(j) = n + c\sqrt{n} + o(\sqrt{n}),
</math>

where <math>h(1) = 1</math>, <math>h(n)</math> is defined to be the smallest exponent appearing in the prime factorization of <math>n > 1</math>, <math>o</math> is [[Big_O_notation#Little-o_notation|little-o notation]], and <math>c = \zeta(\textstyle\frac{3}{2})/\zeta(3)</math>. Consequently,

: <math> \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n h(j) = 1. </math>
